punchline: While his factory burned, Edison sent for his mother and her friends, because they would never see a fire like it again.
thirty_sec: Thomas Edison was sixty-seven when fire swept through his research campus. Years of records and prototypes were gone, and insurance covered about a third of the damage. He told his son to fetch his mother and her friends: they would never see a fire like this again. Three weeks later the factory was partly running, and within a month it worked two shifts. Ryan Holiday sees a man who refused to waste time on despair.
